answer: Withdrawing stake costs a 2% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the ripple fee is applied at the ocean exit, the bridge audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. That is 34 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
